paragraphs: [Yevr.-Arab. I 1689, f. 27r11.] We need to put this bab, together with what follows it, at the head [of our legal exposition]; for it concerns the obligation of baḥth (inquiry) and naẓar (rational reflection),[{2}] and we need it because the latter-day Rabbanites who do engage in naẓar[{3}] — whenever the implications of qiyās (inference by analogy)[{4}] compel them to overturn some position they hold of which we, for our part, disapprove — repudiate qiyās and renounce it, claiming that its application in matters of religious precept is not obligatory. We will report (later, in babs 9 and following) their view and the lines of argument that some of them deploy against qiyās. We are placing first, here, the discussion of the obligation of inquiry, of rational reflection, and of inference by analogy, so that on its basis we may then [f. 27v] proceed to dismantle the position to which they have committed themselves. We already mentioned (in Maqāla I, ṣadr al-kitāb[{5}]) that some of our own co-religionists also repudiate naẓar in matters that fall to reason and rebuke anyone who engages in any of the "outer" sciences,[{6}] and we pledged there to demonstrate the unsoundness of their position and to set forth the soundness of the rational faculty — for it is the principle on which every claim is built, and we therefore begin here by discussing the obligation of inquiry and rational reflection.

We say: the mutakallimūn (the dialectical theologians)[{7}] among the religious communities are divided into several factions[{8}] regarding how knowledge arises: 1. One faction holds that nothing is known except by the senses (al-ḥiss), and that it is impossible to know anything by report (khabar) or by demonstration (istidlāl).[{9}] 2. A second faction holds that one does not know anything by rational reflection, demonstration, or analogy, and that one knows a thing — whether the thing in question is present to the senses or absent — only when one is compelled to its knowledge.[{10}] 3. A third faction holds that knowledge arises only by way of report.[{11}] ---
